decisions.reason: As a core bread product using existing recipes, production routines, and ingredients, it is cheap to keep and there is no clear evidence yet that its value is poor enough to justify withdrawal.
This sweet pastry fits the firm's established confectionery range and can be retained as a low-cost option, though pastry assortments are somewhat easier to rotate if demand proves only average.

The farmhouse bread is close to the core business and inexpensive to continue, but because it overlaps with other breads and has no visible success signal, it has the highest risk of later rationalization.
As a flagship seasonal product with its own page and a gold-award signal, it appears to have revealed strong value and should be kept as part of the firm's focused festive offering.

The premium Christmas stollen also shows positive quality validation through a gold award and fits the firm's heritage-led seasonal business, although it is a bit more expendable than the flagship stollen if the range is simplified.
